Though J specifically is really easy to kneecap because Riposte as an archetype is entirely dependent on how often you get attacked, which is something decided by enemy algorithms and thus not within player initiative
The archetype's power is entirely within the hands of the developers to micromanage instead of something that players can freely interact with
Hence why I feel Riposte is a bit "overpowered" right now in a patch that favors them. Whereas they'll probably be balanced in other patches that aren't tailored to multi hit attacks.

I'd have to see with the next Limited but I personally wouldn't mind them making Limited characters one-size-fits-all when it comes to archetypes, they just need to settle on a design space. Either or is fine. If you design standard characters to be archetype heavy and Limited characters to be flexible, then Limiteds will not be as fomo as they'd be fillers. If you design standard characters to be flexible, you can make Limiteds more archetype heavy as players have an easier time saving.

The problem is they keep switching, so they end up making an archetype heavy Limited in a design space where they were making standard characters archetype heavy, which makes the Limiteds suddenly super FOMO and important. Other way around would work the same.

Bluepoch's inability to keep to a design space, but also their unwillingness to truly experiment, is what's shooting them in the foot. They don't have a solid foundation for their character design, but what is there is all extremely monotone and most players want something more, but without said foundation it is very easy to crash and burn so instead they opt for these 'pseudo-unique' layers to the game like new archetypes cosplaying as old ones and new endgame content
